pr_title: Migrate LIFX to config entry per device
pr_body:
Since there were no tests for this integration, and we are doing a migration, it seemed prudent to get to 100% coverage.  The downside to that is this PR is a bit larger than I had hoped, but at least the majority of the changes by line count is the addition of tests.

## Breaking change

Each LIFX device now has its config entry. The existing entry will be migrated to separate entries automatically as each device is discovered, and will automatically be removed once all devices are found. Migrating to a config entry per device model allows Home Assistant to take care of discovery IP updates and retries, dramatically improving the integration's reliability.

LIFX can now be configured manually by IP address. DHCP, HomeKit, and native discovery are supported for updating IP addresses to ensure we never lose track of a device.

Advanced YAML configuration is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Advanced YAML configuration is no longer necessary as the integration now fully utilizes [Network Configuration](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/network/), and can also function without working discovery.

## Proposed change

Since the LIFX integration currently has discovery reliability issues similar to tplink integration used to have, migrating to a config entry per device model (similar to what is used for other wifi lighting devices like `tplink`, `flux_led`, `wiz`, `nanoleaf`, `wled`, `shelly`, and `yeelight`) which allows Home Assistant to take care of discovery ip updates and retries similar to how we did this for tplink in #56701.

- [x] Lots of tests
- [x] Move the connector into its own module called `aiolifx_connector`, and add a PR for the upstream lib https://github.com/frawau/aiolifx/pull/54 in case they find it useful there as well

# These options are all optional, below are the defaults

    # after getting an acknowledgement before retrying a message if we haven't got a reply yet
    gap_between_ack_and_res: 0.2

    # So with this setting, we retry at 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 1.1, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1, 5.1, 6.1, etc

Just a note: [the `State` reply to any `Set` message set to a bulb that changes the bulb's visible appearance is almost always the _previous_ state of the bulb](https://lan.developer.lifx.com/docs/changing-a-device), i.e. before the change. 

It's better to send a `Set` message with `ack_required=1` and `res_required=0` so you don't get the State response, then send a `GetColor` message afterwards to get the actual current state of the bulb.

This is something that Photons does natively but `aiolifx` appears to be unaware of. I'm assuming it's the reason for the very inefficient and convaluted `set_state` method used to transform the bulbs, when all of that can and should be done in with a single `SetWaveformOptional` message.

issue_context.title: Automatically onboarding DiscoveryFlows breaks  LIFX discovery
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The addition of https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/73841 has broken the LIFX integration discovery for any non-default or non-standard network configuration.

This is pretty simple to replicate too: run Home Assistant 2022.7.0 or later on a host with two NICs, with the default NIC connected to a different subnet than any LIFX bulbs but enable mDNS propagation to that subnet. Home Assistant will enable the LIFX integration automatically, but no bulbs are discovered until the interface on the same subnet as the LIFX devices is enabled in the configuration.

Discovery flow is ignoring the actual function used for discovery, so it's registering false positives. 

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.7.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2022.6.7

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Core

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

Discovery flow should still run the specified function to ensure that the triggered auto-discovery actually results in finding devices on the network as currently configured.
comments:
This is actually already an issue, as the apparently LIFX needs validation, but doesn't right now because it's using the discovery flow.

IMHO this is not an issue resulting from #73841 what you describe can already happen if e.g., mDNS is relayed, but HA can't access the network (in general, regardless of which phase).

If being able to connect is a concern, it should validate that before actually creating the config entry. 

Linked issue #74246 is not related, as #73841 only happens during onboarding, while #74246 is about upgrading (in which a user would already have been onboarded and thus requires confirmation like before).
